name: Carbono Vivo Marañón
description: The Carbono Vivo Marañón Project is a long-term environmental and climate initiative that supports the transition to sustainable land use through the establishment of agroforestry systems based on cashew (Anacardium occidentale) in Colombia. Designed to generate social, environmental, and climate benefits, the PoA brings together producers, processors, marketers, and local communities across the value chain to promote rural development, biodiversity conservation, and carbon removal.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: GS23365 Clean Cooking with Heat Retention Cookers in Cameroon No. 1
description: The Heat Retention Cooking VPA No. 1 aims at distributing around 15,000 to 20,000 heat retention cooking bags, so called “Wonderbags”. These Wonderbags retain a large portion of cooking energy by storing dishes that are brought to the boiling point in a heat insulated bag, where the cooking process is finished without the need of further heating. Therefore, they greatly reduce the consumption of traditional cooking fuels, mainly fuelwood, charcoal and liquified petroleum gas (LPG).
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: The Cameroon Clean Households´ Energy Program

The PoA serves as a framework under which different Voluntary Project Activities (subprojects or “VPAs”) will be implemented.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: MEC - VPA 1 - KP & GB Regions
description:
The Madad Electric Cookstove (MEC) Project is abased clean energy initiative developed by Third Pole Solutions in partnership with the Aga Khan Rural Support Programme (AKRSP) as the coordinating and implementing agency in Pakistan. The project aims to replace traditional wood-burning stoves—locally known as bukhari—and 3-stone cooking methods with energy-efficient electric cookstoves.

The Primary objectives of the Project is to reduce the use of wood for cooking, thereby reducing the GHG emissions and having a positive impact on the Climate (SDG 13). By adopting clean, sustainable cooking practices (SDG7), the Project will focus on ensuring healthy lives and promoting well-being for all by addressing the impact of environment factors on health (SDG3), reduce time spent on collecting or buying firewood resulting in cost savings and increasing the household's disposable income (SDG1) and promote gender equality by involving women's community groups (SDG5)
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Ghana Cocoa Agroforestry Livelihoods Project
description:
The Ghana Cocoa Agroforestry Livelihoods Project is designed to enhance the productivity and long-term sustainability of cocoa farming systems while improving the livelihoods of the communities that depend on them. By introducing an agroforestry model that integrates shade tree species into existing cocoa plantations, the project aims to extend the productive lifespan of cocoa trees and strengthen the system’s resilience to environmental challenges, including pests and diseases. This initiative will be carried out in close partnership with the local communities, with a focus on engaging youth teams to lead on the ground implementation. 
The project is expected to reach 11,000 farmers for an implementation area of 17,000 hectares. The project’s main activity consists of planting shade and fruit trees within the existing cocoa plantations. Nine different native tree species will be incorporated into the farms to achieve a target density of 90 shade trees per hectare. 
Additionally, the new tree plantations will be associated with the training and coaching of the farmers in sustainable agroforestry practices such as tree management, pruning and Integrated Pest Management (IPM). The implementation of these practices is expected to increase the productive lifetime of the cocoa species and reduce the incidence of pests and diseases on the targeted trees. The project is expected to sequester 2.61 MtCO2e within 30 years.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Sterling Improved Cookstoves Carbon Project
description: In most of the countries on the African continent including Ghana, cooking is done on either 3-stone fires or very inefficient traditional cookstoves, consuming a lot of fuel, in particular non-renewable firewood and charcoal. The high biomass consumption has negative impacts on the environment leading to deforestation and land degradation, Greenhouse Gas Emissions (GHG) emissions, loss of soil fertility and soils’ reduced ability of water retention. Further, indoor air pollution through health-damaging pollutants while combusting firewood and charcoal result in diseases like e.g. pneumonia, stroke, ischemic heart diseases, chronic obstructive pulmonary diseases and lung cancer. The purpose of a ‘STERLING IMPROVED COOKSTOVES PROJECT Carbon Project Activities included under the Gold Standard’, is to disseminate highly efficient improved cookstoves (ICS to urban, peri-urban and/or rural users (households, communities, institutions, or SMEs) in Ghana. Several greenhouse gases (GHG), including carbon dioxide, are produced as a result of the incomplete combustion of biomass as used in cook stoves. More GHG emissions result from the use of biomass which is non-renewable. ICS improves heat transfer efficiency as compared to the baseline traditional cook stoves, thereby reducing both the amount of woody biomass used by unit appliances implemented and the emission of GHGs.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Green Horizon: Promoting Sustainable Agroforestry Practices for Enhanced Carbon Sequestration and Improved Smallholder’s Livelihood in India
description:
The project aims to promote agroforestry practices by planting coconut trees (Cocos nucifera) on fallow farmland systems in the Indian state of Karnataka. This coconut plantation initiative falls under the Afforestation and Reforestation (A/R) project activity, focusing on implementing agroforestry practices to enhance the resilience, productivity,
and sustainability of farming systems by enhancing farmer income. 

The project developer Sow & Reap Agro Pvt. Ltd.  aims to achieve the goals of (a) enhancing farmer income through climate resilient systems, and (b) mitigate the impact of climate change by sequestering atmospheric CO2 into coconut tree biomass.

name: Project Saladillo: Sustainable Mosaic Afforestation Operation in Eastern Paraguay
description:
Project Saladillo transforms 15,946 hectares of cattle grazing land, subject to continual slash-and-burn practices, in Paraguay’s Cordillera region into a mosaic plantation combining commercial and conservation forestry. It prioritises long-term ecological resilience and sustainable development. The project integrates 25% permanent conservation with 75% selectively harvested forestry, maintaining at least 96% continuous forest cover. This model prevents deforestation by producing sustainable timber and biomass, while enhancing biodiversity through protection of native forests and riparian corridors, supporting habitat continuity and safeguarding local fauna.
An estimated 1,122,437 tons of CO₂ will be sequestered over 50+ years. High-precision carbon monitoring uses LiDAR-based models calibrated with field sampling to ensure accuracy in both accessible and remote areas.
Saladillo generates formal, year-round employment through staggered planting and harvesting, eliminating informal labour, reducing seasonal risks, and ensuring steady income for local communities. It collaborates closely with local NGOs such as Fundación Moisés Bertoni and the University of Asunción, integrating community engagement, biodiversity monitoring, and academic research.
The project adheres to the highest environmental and social safeguards, aligning with FSC certification, IFC Performance Standards, and World Bank guidelines, contributing to SDGs 8, 12, 13, and 15.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Enhancing Climate Resilience and Rural Livelihoods through Plantation Project by Infosys
description: The proposed project is a Voluntary Project Activity (VPA) focused on afforestation and will be implemented in Odisha, India. It aims to sequester atmospheric carbon dioxide through plantations. The project will promote native and climate-resilient species, with the special emphasis to support sustainable livelihoods through community participation and agroforestry practices. It will also enhance biodiversity and improve soil health. Furthermore, the project generates temporary employment for local communities during the implementation and management of the plantation. The project aligns with multiple SDGs, including climate action, life on land, and no poverty.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: GS23355 VPA01 Oyu - Ubuntu Borehole Revival
description:
The project aims to restore and maintain non-functional boreholes in rural, water-scarce regions of South Africa. By providing reliable access to clean groundwater, it reduces dependence on unsafe water sources and the need to boil water using traditional fuels. The initiative also builds local capacity by training and employing community technicians for ongoing maintenance, ensuring long-term sustainability and resilience.

The project improves access to safe drinking water, leading to a reduction in waterborne diseases and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the use of traditional fuels for water purification. It lessens the burden on women and children by minimizing the time spent collecting water, enhances community health and safety, creates local employment opportunities, and promotes awareness of safe water and hygiene practices.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: GS23156-GS13112 RVPA-1 VPA-11 Improved Rice Cultivation in Bangladesh
description: The VPA aims to positively impact the livelihoods of farmers in Bangladesh by promoting the adoption of the Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) method in rice cultivation. This improved farming practice replaces the traditional continuous flooding technique, which contributes to significant greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions due to methane release from waterlogged fields. The AWD method optimizes water usage by alternating periods of wetting and drying, which not only reduces water consumption but also enhances soil aeration, improving nutrient uptake. As a result, the activity substantially reduces methane emissions, leading to lower overall GHG emissions. By introducing AWD practice, the activity supports sustainable water management and environmental sustainability in the region. Bangladesh Bondhu Foundation is the Project Developer as well as the VPA Implementer for this Program of Activity. Climate Secure serves as the CME.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
